craft_notes: Sthāyin: no-twoness (wish alone divides). Rows: row 2 (nowhere→split). Close: split (bheda as landing: the split IS the sentence's end). Rejected: 'nonduality' named — kept no-twoness (the verse denies, never names); 'desire' for wish — kept wish (icchā precise).

lines: I, you; you, I — so no twoness of us anywhere.
Mere wish to seize samādhi: that is all the abiding of split is.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ tvaṃ tvamahaṃ ceti bhinnatā nāvayoḥ kvacit | samādhigrahaṇecchāyā bhedasyāvasthitirhyasau

reads_against.argmap: Is there duality? → Non-duality asserted, difference explained away: what looks like abiding difference is only the wish to grasp samādhi.
c1_essence: Non-duality asserted, difference explained as the wish to grasp samādhi.
